text: The discovery that postsynaptic scaffold proteins such as Shank and Homer are present in sponges, which have no synapses, is best interpreted as evidence that:
choices: Sponges secretly possess synapses that had escaped detection
The molecular toolkit for building the synapse predates the synapse itself
These scaffold proteins are nonfunctional evolutionary relics in sponges
explanation: Sakarya et al. (2007) showed the postsynaptic scaffold predates the animal kingdom, supporting the view that the synapse was assembled from pre-existing molecular components rather than invented wholesale. Sponges genuinely lack synapses and neurons, and the proteins are functional signaling components in sponges, not relics.
